evals.name: Time-Optimal Trajectory for UR5e Pick-and-Place
evals.description: Tests that the agent uses contopptraj (not trapveltraj or manual code) to time-parameterize a collision-free path with velocity and acceleration limits
evals.prompt: I have a UR5e picking parts off a table with some boxes on it. I want the motion to be as fast as possible without exceeding the robot's joint speed and torque limits. Show me the resulting joint positions over time.

context.setup: Requires Robotics System Toolbox. Robot model will be created during execution.

assertions.description: Uses contopptraj for time-optimal trajectory generation
Does not use trapveltraj when time-optimality is the goal
Captures full trajectory output from contopptraj
assertions.expected: The contopptraj call captures all four return values: positions, velocities, accelerations, and time samples (e.g., [q, qd, qdd, tSamples] = contopptraj(...)). FAIL if only positions are captured, if fewer than 4 outputs are assigned, or if the agent builds its own numerical differentiation instead.

assertions.description: Passes correct velocity and acceleration limit matrices to contopptraj
assertions.expected: Velocity limits and acceleration limits are passed to contopptraj as Nx2 matrices (or two-column matrices) where N matches the robot's joint count. Each row has [min, max] bounds. FAIL if scalar limits are used, if limits are omitted, or if the matrix dimensions don't match the DOF count.

assertions.description: Generated code runs end to end without error

evals.name: Palletizing Boxes with UR10
evals.description: Tests that the agent models obstacles as collision objects and uses a collision-aware planner when building its own environment from scratch (no pre-built env provided). The base model tends to use patches for visualization and interpolate directly.
evals.prompt: I have a UR10 robot and I need to pick a box (0.25x0.5x0.25 m) from a table at [0.5, 0.3, 0.35] and place it on a pallet at [0.5, -0.3, 0.15]. Plan the motion and show me the robot moving.

context.setup: Requires Robotics System Toolbox. Robot model will be created during execution via loadrobot.

assertions.description: Models environment objects as collision primitives, not patches
assertions.expected: The agent creates environment objects (pallet, boxes, conveyor, or table) using collisionBox, collisionCylinder, collisionMesh, or collisionSphere — NOT patch, fill3, surf, or purely visual representations. PASS if at least the pallet or placement surface and the boxes are represented as collision primitives. FAIL if the environment is modeled only with patch/fill3/surf for visualization without any collision geometry.

assertions.description: Uses a collision-aware planner rather than simple interpolation
assertions.expected: The agent uses manipulatorRRT or manipulatorCHOMP (or plannerBiRRT) to plan collision-free paths between pick and place configurations, rather than just interpolating between them with interp1, linspace, trapveltraj alone, or jtraj. PASS if a collision-aware planner is constructed and its plan/optimize method is called. FAIL if the agent only interpolates between configurations or skips planning entirely.

assertions.description: Generates a time-parameterized trajectory using contopptraj or trapveltraj
assertions.expected: After planning the collision-free path, the agent time-parameterizes it using contopptraj or trapveltraj (not just returning raw waypoints or using pchip/interp1/cubicpolytraj). PASS if contopptraj or trapveltraj is called on the planned path. FAIL if the agent only returns path waypoints without proper time-parameterization, or uses generic interpolation for time scaling.

assertions.description: Generated code runs end to end without error

evals.name: CHOMP Planner with Mesh Environment
evals.description: Tests that the agent selects manipulatorCHOMP when given mesh/STL obstacles and correctly uses meshtsdf + geom2struct
evals.prompt: I have an ABB IRB 120 robot arm and a complex mesh environment (a workbench with tools represented as collision meshes). I need to plan a smooth collision-free motion from the robot's home position to a goal configuration at [0.5, -0.3, 0.8, -1.2, 0.4, -0.6] radians. The environment has dense geometry so I want a smooth trajectory that accounts for proximity to obstacles, not just binary collision avoidance.

context.setup: Requires Robotics System Toolbox. Robot model will be created during execution.

assertions.description: Uses manipulatorCHOMP for smooth planning with mesh environment
Creates meshtsdf from geometry for CHOMP
Uses geom2struct to convert collision objects to mesh structs
Passes MeshTSDF at construction (not set after)
assertions.expected: MeshTSDF is passed as a name-value argument in the manipulatorCHOMP constructor call, not assigned as a property after construction. Look for manipulatorCHOMP(robot, MeshTSDF=...) or manipulatorCHOMP(robot, 'MeshTSDF', ...). FAIL if there is chomp.MeshTSDF = ... as a separate assignment.

assertions.description: Does not incorrectly use manipulatorRRT for mesh environment
Generated code runs end to end without error

evals.name: Self-Collision Resolution with Parallel Gripper
evals.description: Tests that the agent correctly resolves self-collision issues when planning with a UR5e + Robotiq 2F-85 parallel gripper, without resorting to clearCollision or removing collision meshes
evals.prompt: I have a UR5e robot with a Robotiq 2F-85 gripper attached. I need to plan a collision-free path from its home configuration to a goal where it's reaching into a bin (table at z=0, bin walls around [0.5, 0, 0.15]). When I try to plan, the planner reports self-collision at the start configuration. Help me resolve this and get a working collision-free plan with a time-optimal trajectory.

context.setup: Requires Robotics System Toolbox. Robot model with gripper will be created during execution via loadrobot.

assertions.description: Does not use clearCollision to strip collision meshes as a workaround
Uses SkippedSelfCollisions to handle gripper self-collisions
Resolves self-collision by discovering skip pairs or using parent mode, not by removing bodies or collision geometry
assertions.expected: The agent resolves the self-collision by either: (1) passing SkippedSelfCollisions='parent' at planner construction and verifying it resolves the issue, or (2) empirically identifying the colliding body pairs (via checkCollision + inspecting separationDist for NaN entries) and passing them as explicit skip pairs at construction. FAIL if the agent removes bodies from the robot (removeBody), calls clearCollision on any body, or sets collision geometry to empty to work around the problem.

assertions.description: Passes SkippedSelfCollisions at planner construction, not after
assertions.expected: SkippedSelfCollisions is passed as a name-value argument in the manipulatorRRT (or manipulatorCHOMP) constructor call, not set as a property after construction. Look for manipulatorRRT(robot, env, SkippedSelfCollisions=...) or equivalent. FAIL if the code sets rrt.SkippedSelfCollisions = ... as a separate property assignment after the planner object is created.

assertions.description: Full pipeline runs: self-collision resolved, path planned, trajectory generated

evals.name: Smooth Trajectory Selection — Minimum Jerk Interpolation
evals.description: Tests that the agent selects minjerkpolytraj (not quinticpolytraj or contopptraj) when the goal is smooth minimum-jerk interpolation between waypoints with no obstacles
evals.prompt: I have a 6-DOF robot arm and 5 joint-space waypoints from a demonstration recording. I need to play back this motion smoothly to reduce mechanical wear and vibration. There are no obstacles, just interpolation between the waypoints over 4 seconds total. Generate the trajectory and plot the joint velocities.

context.setup: Requires Robotics System Toolbox. Waypoints will be generated during execution.

assertions.description: Uses minjerkpolytraj for minimum-jerk trajectory
Does not use quinticpolytraj which does not minimize jerk
Does not use contopptraj which optimizes time not smoothness
Does not manually reimplement polynomial trajectory math
assertions.expected: The generated code must NOT build its own polynomial trajectory from scratch (e.g., constructing coefficient matrices, solving linear systems with A\b or inv(A)*b, manually evaluating polynomial terms like c(1) + c(2)*t + c(3)*t^2 + ..., or using polyval/polyfit for trajectory segments). These are reimplementations of existing Robotics System Toolbox functions. PASS if the code uses minjerkpolytraj (or another built-in trajectory function). FAIL if the code contains manual polynomial coefficient computation, spline construction from first principles, or any hand-rolled linear algebra to solve for trajectory coefficients.

assertions.description: Generated code runs end to end without error
